page_title: L2MAC: Large Language Model Automatic Computer for Extensive Code Generation

sources.entry: Paper - L2MAC: Large Language Model Automatic Computer for Extensive Code Generation

summary.name: L2MAC
summary.one_liner: L2MAC is an LLM-based multi-agent framework, described as a stored-program automatic computer, for generating long and consistent outputs such as large codebases or entire books.
use_cases: generating large codebases for system design tasks
producing long coherent text such as a book
multi-step code generation beyond a context window
summary.what_it_does: The paper presents L2MAC, which it describes as the first practical LLM-based general-purpose stored-program automatic computer framework. Its memory has two parts: an instruction registry holding a prompt program for the user's task, and a file store for final and intermediate outputs. Each instruction is executed by a separate LLM agent, with a control unit managing that agent's context and reading and writing the file store. The authors state that L2MAC achieves state-of-the-art performance on generating large codebases for system design tasks and also works for extensive text tasks such as writing an entire book. The page is the arXiv abstract listing (v1 submitted October 2023, latest revision June 2025) and does not include details of the implementation.
notable: Memory split into an instruction registry and a file store, modeled on a von Neumann architecture
Each instruction executed by a separate LLM agent with a control unit managing context
Claims to bypass finite context window limits for long outputs
caveats: Page is an arXiv abstract; no software release, pricing or installation details are stated
Performance claims are the authors' own empirical results
